key_findings.finding: The card entity card1=9917 has an extensive history (905 prior transactions) with a mature fraud rate of 37.31%, roughly 10x the ~3.5% population base rate — a strongly established fraud pattern, not a new/thin entity.
Maximal gang signal: gang_score=1.0 for card1=9917, with high fan-out across 134 devices, 13 emails, and 10 addr1 values — consistent with a card cycling through a device farm.

The card1+device co-pattern has a 100% mature fraud rate, and the transaction hits rule R_PRIOR_FRAUD_CARD1_DEVICE (historical 21.04%, 6x lift). This is the single strongest signal on the transaction.

Three of four retrieved similar cases (#3459639, #3458397, #3388914) are confirmed fraud (chargebacks) with a near-identical fingerprint to this transaction (ProductCD=C, visa/debit, gmail.com, card1=9917, small amount $12-29). One case (#3414738) was a manually-cleared high-scoring false positive with the same profile, so profile-match alone is not decisive — but the entity's mature fraud history resolves the ambiguity toward fraud.

The transaction's own attributes are mid-risk contributors: ProductCD=C (mature fraud rate 11.38%, ~3.2x base) and DeviceType=mobile (rule lift 2.8x); the gmail.com email domain is near-baseline (4.36%) and not itself a signal.

CONFLICT with upstream model: GBDT p=0.5771 materially understates risk. The entity-level mature fraud rate (37.31%) and card1+device fraud rate (100%) indicate this transaction is far riskier than a coin-flip score implies.

gang_association.rationale: gang_score=1.0 combined with device fan-out of 134 (plus 13 emails / 10 addresses) on a single card, an entity-level mature fraud rate of 37.31%, and a 100% card1+device fraud rate, is a textbook coordinated device-farm fraud ring. Multiple confirmed-fraud historical cases share this exact card1.

report.disposition_rationale: Under the expected-cost framework, this is small ($21.70) but sits on a confirmed gang entity (gang_score=1.0, 37% mature fraud rate, 100% card1+device fraud, fan-out 134). Escalation/entity freeze ($40) is justified even at small amount because it stops future batch fraud from this ring — far more valuable than declining this single low-value transaction. A plain decline would only stop this $21.70 while leaving the ring active.
report.summary: Transaction 3555324 ($21.70, ProductCD=C, visa/debit, gmail, mobile SM-J701M) is tied to card1=9917, a heavily-used entity (905 priors) with a 37.31% mature fraud rate, maximal gang_score (1.0), device fan-out of 134, and a 100% card1+device fraud rate. Three of four look-alike historical cases on this same card are confirmed chargeback fraud (one high-score false positive existed but the entity's own fraud history overrides that ambiguity). The GBDT score of 0.5771 understates the true risk. This is a coordinated device-farm ring; despite the tiny amount, the recommended action is escalate to freeze the entity and halt batch fraud.
